text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Socialist Edek decides its chairman Vassos Lyssarides should run in presidential elections in 1998.
- U.S. President Bill Clinton avoids reference to the Cyprus problem in his state address, confirming information of second thoughts of an initiative on Cyprus.
- The cabinet approves improvements on shop opening hours, extending them by one hour.
- The time is not yet right for direct talks, says U.N. envoy Han Sung-joo.
- The government announces a 10 million pound "feel good" package of incentives to boost exports.

- Communist Akel criticises President Glafcos Clerides for "misleading" references to the operation of the National Council. President Clerides undermines the function, says Akel general secretary Demetris Christofias.
- Frost on crops causes damages worth millions of pounds throughout Cyprus.
- The government announces a series of incentives to help the economy.
- UN envoy says if a solution to the Cyprus problem is not found now the situation will get worse.
